content.title: Why Do Jews Celebrate Passover? | The History of the Exodus
content.text: Passover is one of the most important holidays in Judaism, commemorating the Biblical story of the Exodus when the Israelites escaped slavery in Egypt. But what exactly is Passover, and how did the traditions surrounding the holiday develop? In this video, a history professor explains the origins of Passover, the story of the Exodus, and the meaning behind the Seder meal that Jewish families celebrate each year. We explore the historical background of the holiday, the symbolism of foods like matzah and bitter herbs, and how the Passover Seder retells the story of liberation from generation to generation. You’ll learn: • The historical origins of Passover • The Biblical story of the Exodus from Egypt • What happens during a Passover Seder • The meaning behind matzah, bitter herbs, and other traditions • Why Passover remains central to Jewish identity today Passover is both a religious and historical commemoration that has shaped Jewish culture for thousands of years. Understanding its origins helps explain why the story of freedom told during Passover continues to resonate around the world today.
